clue.text: Need an alternative to the Muses, for example

definitions.note: the nine Muses of Greek myth make a set of nine, one example of such a group

indicators.note: an alternative version of these words is a different arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone wants a different source of inspiration from the classical Muses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' signals rearranging NEED and AN. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a group of nine, and the Muses numbered nine, so they are an example of one.

clue.text: Incorruptible Queen's name amid the raised dead

indicators.note: amid means the following pieces sit in the middle of the next one
in a down clue, raised means a word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the late person is one who has died
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A queen's name is spoken of as undying among those who have died.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen; the dead are 'the late'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incorruptible never decays, so it lasts for ever: a synonym in the sense of everlasting.

clue.text: Alternately into hockey and hanky-panky

indicators.note: alternately tells you to take every other letter of the following words

explanation.surface: Some sports players mix their game with romantic mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternately' picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of INTO HOCKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for sexual activity, so they are slang synonyms.

clue.text: A partner reflects: "Rugby Union used to be"

definitions.text: A partner reflects: "Rugby Union used to be"

parts.note: a mate is a partner or companion

indicators.note: reflects means the letters are mirrored, read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone's partner muses that rugby union was once unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflects' turns RU into UR. Rugby Union was officially unpaid until it went professional in 1995, so the whole clue also gives the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby Union was for over a century played by unpaid sportsmen, so the clue describes the sport's former non-professional status.

clue.text: Medic admitting abduction of tradesman

indicators.note: admitting means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
rape has an old sense of carrying off by force, as in The Rape of the Sabine Women

explanation.surface: A doctor confesses to kidnapping a shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The older sense of 'rape' is seizure or carrying off by force, which the clue's 'abduction' relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: A draper is a seller of cloth, a kind of shopkeeper or merchant.

clue.text: Excellent fellows wearing right clothes

indicators.note: wearing means one piece goes around the others like a garment

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI in crosswords
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Fine gentlemen are dressed in proper attire.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-class, is written AI in crosswords by letter-for-number play.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a literary word for garments or clothing, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Somehow copes with tent at festival

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone manages with a tent at a music festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges COPES and TENT. 'with' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitsun, the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter, is a religious festival.

clue.text: Lads' language

parts.note: two lads, boys named Russ and Ian, together give their names
two lads, boys named Russ and Ian, together give their names

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lads'' is plural: two boys' names, Russ and Ian, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Slavonic tongue spoken in Russia, a language.

clue.text: Snake taking shelter when at rest

indicators.note: taking means the first piece takes the second into itself

parts.note: an asp is a small venomous snake
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A snake hides in shelter when resting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; the lee is the side sheltered from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is at rest, so the two are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: So his Jews haven't converted?

indicators.note: converted means the letters are changed into another form

explanation.surface: A question whether a man's Jewish relatives have changed religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges SO HIS JEWS HAVEN'T. The whole clue also hints at people who have converted to this faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this Christian denomination are often converts, so the clue suggests that those Jews have converted to it.

clue.text: Catalyst stimulating Fritz's ultimate enemy

indicators.note: stimulating means stirring the letters up into a new order
ultimate means taking the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something spurs a German soldier's foe into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' picks Z from FRITZ'S, and 'stimulating' rearranges it with ENEMY.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a protein that speeds up biochemical reactions, a biological catalyst.

clue.text: River on which servicemen absorb points for interpretation

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England

indicators.note: absorb means the servicemen take the points into themselves

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Soldiers on a river take in points for analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a Devon river; 'on which' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is critical explanation of a text, especially scripture, so it is a scholarly interpretation.

clue.text: Inverts catch VD? Nonsense

indicators.note: inverts means the two following pieces are put in the opposite order

parts.note: clap is slang for gonorrhoea, a venereal disease
to trap something is to catch it

explanation.surface: Read as a medical question, someone asks whether inverts can contract a venereal disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inverts' swaps the clue order of 'catch' and 'VD' rather than reversing letters; it masquerades as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious empty talk, rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Hold forth about origin of fast puncture

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to perorate is to speak at length, to hold forth

indicators.note: origin of means taking the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone lectures on the start of a quick tyre puncture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin of' picks F from FAST, and 'about' puts PERORATE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To perforate is to pierce holes in something, to puncture it.

clue.text: Difficult time to get aroused

parts.note: horny is slang for sexually aroused

explanation.surface: It is an awkward moment to become excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is a prickly, hard one, so the word means difficult.

clue.text: No place for hedonists seeking culture in Bath

indicators.note: in means the culture piece is set inside the Bath piece

parts.note: Bath is an English spa town, so it is a spa
art is culture

explanation.surface: Pleasure-seekers go to the city of Bath for culture.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Roman spa city in south-west England; 'seeking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Sparta was famed for austere military discipline, the opposite of a pleasure-seeker's haven.

clue.text: Film starting before the last one?

definitions.text: Film starting before the last one?

parts.words: Film starting before the last one?
parts.note: a film whose story begins before that of the previous film in the series, even though it was made later

explanation.definitionFit: A prequel tells events earlier than an existing story, so its plot starts before the earlier film.

clue.text: Not beginning final journey on horseback, perhaps

indicators.note: not beginning means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: last means final
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone, not quite starting a final ride, sits on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not beginning' drops L from LAST RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on each side, as on a horse, is one example of the posture.

clue.text: Guru protecting wrecked boat from malicious interference

indicators.note: protecting means the guru wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a sage is a wise teacher, a guru

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A guru guards a wrecked boat from vandals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link; 'Guru' looks like the subject but supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate damage or obstruction meant to cause harm is the meaning, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Commit minor offence with obnoxious gas rising from backside?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas used in riot control
the rump is the backside

explanation.surface: A rude joke about flatulence as a petty crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns CS into SC. In Britain to scrump is to steal apples from an orchard; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumping, pilfering fruit from orchards, is a classic minor childhood offence.

clue.text: Brought up to burgle and thieve heartlessly, winding up here

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to rob is to burgle

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: to steal is to thieve

explanation.surface: A youth raised to burgle and steal ends up in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' turns ROB into BOR; 'heartlessly' drops the middle E of STEAL. A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Young criminals were sent to such an institution, so it is where a delinquent would end up.

clue.text: Force to sign with pleasure

definitions.note: used as a verb, to give pleasure to

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravitational force, as in g-force
to ratify a treaty is to sign it

explanation.surface: Someone is compelled to sign a contract, but happily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pleasure' is used here as a verb meaning to please; 'to' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To gratify someone is to please or satisfy them, the verb sense of the definition.

clue.text: Bearer of news about the comic relief in Macbeth?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the drunken Porter provides the comic scene in Shakespeare's Macbeth

explanation.surface: A messenger talks of the funny scene in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Porter's knocking scene is famous comic relief amid the tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist gathers and relays news, so is a bearer of it.

clue.text: Have a good time, taking in a show

indicators.note: taking in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to revel is to make merry, have a good time

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys themselves at a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts A inside REVEL. 'show' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show or disclose it, a synonym.

clue.text: Locations abandoned by Oriental deity

indicators.note: abandoned by means the following letter leaves the word

parts.note: venues are locations for events
E stands for East, Oriental

explanation.surface: Places deserted by an Eastern god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' drops E from VENUES.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Roman goddess of love, so a deity.

clue.text: Dog is eating a short dog and is being treated accordingly

indicators.note: eating means the dog piece takes something inside it

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog is devouring a smaller dog while being dealt with likewise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means 'with the necessary changes having been made'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means with the necessary changes made, so each case is handled in its own fitting way.

clue.text: Editorial report on songs

indicators.note: report means something spoken and heard, so a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper editorial

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial reports on music.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is the British term for a newspaper's main opinion article. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These are German art songs, such as those of Schubert, so the plural fits songs.

clue.text: Vessel, earthbound but posh

indicators.note: bound means the earth piece encloses the other

parts.note: clay is a kind of earth
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship that never leaves land is nonetheless upmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earthbound' looks like one word meaning grounded, but splits into 'earth' and 'bound'; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Classy means stylish and high-quality, informally synonymous with posh.
